issues.evidence: The arithmetic is right ($76,000 / 365 = $208.22). But OPWDD's report says its Medicaid spend is about $10 billion, 'about $76,000 per person' across ALL services, for 135,000+ people, with 35% children and 7% seniors. That spend includes care coordination, day, community habilitation and respite. Certified residential alone is $5.9B. IRA residents are the highest-cost group, so the all-services average is not a valid proxy for a supervised-IRA per diem.
issues.fix: Unverifiable from the cited source. Replace the benchmark with the published DOH/OPWDD supervised-IRA per diem for the target region, or with a written rate from OPWDD/DOH. All revenue lines and every profit result depend on this figure.

issues.json_path: staffing.ira4[0], staffing.ira6[0], staffing.ira8[0], staffing.ira6x2[0], staffing.ira8x2[0], staffing.ira8x3[0] (DSP hours)
issues.current: Zero staff for about 130 h/month on weekday day-program hours
issues.correct: Staff must be onsite or proximately available at all times any resident is present
issues.evidence: 14 NYCRR 686.99: a supervised IRA 'has staff onsite or proximately available at all times when the persons are present'. The model schedules no staff when residents are away at day programs. It has no coverage for sick days, day-program closures, retirement-age residents or hospital returns, when residents are home on weekdays.
issues.fix: Add coverage hours for weekday residents at home, or document that the day-program assumption holds for every resident. Also add a relief factor. The hours shown are post-coverage hours, not paid hours, so they exclude sick leave, training and overtime.

issues.correct: Add explicit lines for NY statutory disability (DBL) coverage, NY Paid Sick Leave and overtime
issues.evidence: The notes cover only FICA, UI, FUTA, workers' comp and a generic 'benefits 8%'. They do not mention NY DBL coverage, which employers must carry. They do not mention NY Paid Sick Leave (paid hours are required for most employers). They do not mention overtime premium for 24/7 residential shifts or paid mandatory annual training time (14 NYCRR 633.8). NY Paid Family Leave is employee-funded through a 0.432% payroll deduction, so it is not an employer cost.
issues.fix: Add a DBL premium line, a paid-sick-leave and training-time hours allowance, and an overtime or relief-staff factor. Confirm each rate with a NY payroll or insurance broker. This could not be fully checked from the cited sources.
